14	CASE OD2-HO-OBVWRONG-2 (OBVWRONG, cross-domain): Harlow Bay: the bag rate that doubled the month the handler changed
15	Setting: Harlow Bay International is a mid-sized fictional airport. Its baggage handling system and manual encode desk are run by the Harlow Bay Airport Authority (HBAA). Corvane Air is the largest carrier at the station. On 1 September Corvane's ramp handling, and Pelion Airways' ramp handling, moved from Quillon Ramp Services to Tessaly Ground. Departing bags pass through automatic tag reader arrays. Bags whose tags cannot be read are diverted to a manual encode desk and then sent on to the make-up laterals, where handler crews load carts that close 35 minutes before departure.
16	Presenting request: Corvane's VP Ground Operations plans to issue Tessaly Ground a formal breach notice this Friday. Before that, the steering group has asked you to work out why Corvane's departing-bag mishandling rate at Harlow Bay nearly doubled from September and to recommend what to do next.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Corvane Air station performance dashboard, Harlow Bay, extract dated 4 Nov (system-record): Departing bags not carried on the booked flight, per 1,000 departing passengers: Jun 4.0, Jul 4.1, Aug 4.1, Sep 7.6, Oct 7.9. Departing passengers: Jun 205,000; Jul 212,000; Aug 219,000; Sep 188,000; Oct 176,000. Corvane network average excluding Harlow Bay: between 3.9 and 4.2 in every month. On-time departures within 15 minutes: Aug 81%, Sep 77%, Oct 78%. Annotation by station office: 'Ground handling transferred from Quillon Ramp Services to Tessaly Ground, 1 Sep.' No other annotations on the dashboard.
19	E2 [stage S1] Email from Dana Orlov, Corvane Station Manager, to Martin Achterberg, 5 Nov (manager-account): Martin, the rate sat at about 4 for over a year under Quillon and nearly doubled the month Tessaly took over. Their crews are green. I have personally watched bags sitting on a lateral with nobody working the cart. Tessaly keep blaming 'the airport system' and the encode desk, but that is the same desk Quillon worked with for six years without complaint. The two new evening departures add some pressure, but we ran heavier banks every summer. I recommend a formal breach notice and withholding the performance element of the fee until the rate is back under 4.5. Dana
20	E3 [stage S1] Tessaly Ground monthly staffing return to Corvane, 31 Oct (document): Harlow Bay ramp headcount: 164 (contract minimum 160). Staff with under six months' airside experience: 67 (41%). Comparator from Quillon's final return, 31 Aug: headcount 152, of whom 18 (12%) had under six months. 23 former Quillon loaders transferred to Tessaly. Shift fill rate, Sep–Oct: early 97%, late 94%, evening 89%. Crewing model: a single Harlow Bay crew pool covers all Tessaly-handled turns (Corvane Air and Pelion Airways), assigned by the shift lead. Tessaly also staffs Corvane's baggage service desk under the same contract.
21	E4 [stage S1] Minutes, Corvane–Tessaly weekly operations review, 29 Oct (document): Present: D. Orlov (Corvane), P. Venn (Tessaly ops lead), two Corvane duty managers. HBAA was invited but did not attend. 1. Mishandling: P. Venn said 'a lot of our late bags come down from the manual encode station after the lateral has closed' and asked Corvane to raise encode delays with HBAA. D. Orlov replied that the encode desk is unchanged and that crews should sweep laterals before closing carts. 2. Schedule: Corvane 418 and Corvane 422 added to the evening bank from 1 Sep; no change to lateral closing times. 3. Actions: Tessaly to submit a crew retraining plan by 12 Nov; Corvane to circulate the October dashboard.
22	E5 [stage S1] Corvane IT helpdesk ticket summary, bag-tag printers, Harlow Bay, 1 Aug–31 Oct (log): Weekly tickets categorised 'tag printer jam/misfeed' (kiosks and counters combined): August weekly average 5; September–October weekly average 13. Context notes appended by helpdesk: (a) Procurement (L. Sato): from 1 Sep all Harlow Bay counters and kiosks switched from Brackwater Print tag stock to Fennick Labels stock under a new contract, unit cost down 18%. The Brackwater contract remains valid to 31 Dec, and about five weeks of Brackwater stock is held in station stores. (b) The kiosk maintenance vendor moved kiosk printer preventive cleaning from weekly to fortnightly from 1 Sep; counter printers are maintained by Corvane IT, schedule unchanged. (c) No printer configuration changes recorded since June.
23	E6 [stage S1] Message from Martin Achterberg, Corvane VP Ground Operations, to the Harlow Bay steering group, 6 Nov (leadership-account): I've read Dana's note and I agree with it. We changed one thing on 1 September, the handler, and the mishandling rate nearly doubled. Tessaly bid low, staffed up with new hires, and is now pointing at the airport's IT. I want a breach notice drafted for my signature by Friday and the performance payment held. If anyone has evidence that this is not a handling problem, bring it to me before then. Otherwise we proceed.
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Tessaly Ground training and certification records, Harlow Bay ramp staff, Sep–Oct - Tessaly Ground HR / Corvane quality audit (document): All 164 ramp staff hold current airside passes and loading certification. The 67 staff with under six months' experience completed Tessaly's five-day ramp course and at least ten supervised turns before being rostered solo. Nine staff are overdue a 12-month refresher module, all of them ex-Quillon transfers. Two recordable bag-handling incidents in Sep–Oct (a bag dropped at a hold door; a cart overturned in wind), neither involving a lost bag. Corvane quality audited the training records on 20 Oct: no major findings.
26	C2 [stage S1] Corvane customer complaints and delayed-baggage compensation, Harlow Bay departures, Aug–Oct - Corvane customer relations (financial-record): Delayed-baggage complaints from passengers departing Harlow Bay: Aug 312, Sep 588, Oct 611. Interim-expense compensation paid: Aug €21,400; Sep €44,900; Oct €47,300. Typical complaint narratives: the bag arrived on the next day's flight, and destination agents said it 'was left at Harlow Bay'. Twelve complaints mention rude staff at Harlow Bay check-in. Median delay before the bag reached the passenger: 26 hours, unchanged from August.
27	C3 [stage S1] Tessaly Ground internal ramp audit reports, Harlow Bay, Sep–Oct - Tessaly Ground quality team (document): 48 turn audits. Procedural compliance score: Sep 88%, Oct 93%. Recurring findings: hold-door bag counts not signed (Sep, 7 turns); laterals not swept before cart closure on the evening bank (Sep 5 turns, Oct 2 turns); cart curtains left open (4 turns). Auditor's comment: 'Evening bank crews frequently receive late encode bags after carts are closed; crews have been instructed to radio for a hold where possible.' No comparison with the Quillon period is available.
28	C4 [stage S1] HBAA baggage reconciliation data by carrier and routing path, Harlow Bay departures, Jul–Oct - Harlow Bay Airport Authority baggage reconciliation system (system-record): HBAA baggage reconciliation extract, Harlow Bay departures, Jul–Oct. Bags not carried on the booked flight, per 1,000 departing passengers. Corvane: Jul 4.1, Aug 4.1, Sep 7.6, Oct 7.9. Pelion Airways (about 70% of Corvane's volume): 3.6, 3.8, 3.7, 3.6. Both carriers moved from Quillon to Tessaly on 1 Sep and are worked from Tessaly's single crew pool. Corvane by routing path: auto-read bags 3.9, 3.9, 3.8, 3.7; manual-encode bags 0.2, 0.2, 3.8, 4.2. Corvane bags diverted to manual encode, daily average: Aug 70, Sep 455, Oct 470. Evening-bank median encode dwell: Aug 7 min, Sep 29, Oct 33. Of the Corvane encode-path bags not carried, 91% reached the make-up lateral after its scheduled closing time. The check-in time profile of encode-path bags matches that of auto-read bags.
29	C5 [stage S1] HBAA sortation system maintenance log, tag reader arrays 1–4, Jul–Oct - Harlow Bay Airport Authority engineering (log): Planned maintenance: fortnightly lens cleaning on all four arrays, completed on schedule. The log records work performed. It does not record read rates.
30	C6 [stage S1] Corvane Harlow Bay departure schedule and baggage lateral times, Aug vs Sep–Oct - Corvane network planning (document): Evening bank (17:00–21:00) departures: August 9 per day; from 1 Sep 11 per day (Corvane 418 and 422 added). Lateral opening: three hours before departure; lateral closing: 35 minutes before departure for all flights, unchanged. Daytime departures unchanged at 23 per day.
31	C7 [stage S1] Fennick Labels certificate of conformance and supplier cover letter, 4 Nov - Fennick Labels account manager (vendor-account): Certificate: batches FL-2207 to FL-2215 tested by Fennick's in-house laboratory against Corvane tag specification rev. 6; adhesive, tear strength and thermal sensitivity 'within specification'. We would welcome a joint trial and are confident print quality will be resolved by adjusting your printer settings.' No third-party test results are attached.
32	C8 [stage S1] Teyra Systems technical bulletin TB-31 on thermal media settings for bag-tag printers - Teyra Systems (printer manufacturer) (vendor-account): General bulletin, issued 2023: 'Direct thermal media differ in activation energy. When changing media supplier, customers should print test tags and verify barcode grade before deployment. Low-sensitivity media may require darkness +2 to +4 and reduced print speed.' The bulletin names no media supplier and contains no data on Fennick or Brackwater stock. It also notes that print-head wear reduces barcode contrast.
33	C9 [stage S1] HBAA automatic tag reader statistics by tag range, arrays 1–4, 1 Aug–31 Oct - Harlow Bay Airport Authority baggage systems (T. Rhee, engineer) (telemetry): HBAA automatic tag reader statistics, arrays 1–4, 1 Aug–31 Oct, by tag number range. No-read rate (bag diverted to manual encode): Corvane tags issued at Harlow Bay in August (Brackwater stock) 1.5%; issued Sep–Oct (Fennick stock) 11.8%, of which counters 11.5% and kiosks 12.0%. Corvane transfer tags issued at other stations 1.4%; Pelion tags 1.3%. Transfer and Pelion rates stay within 0.3 points on every array, including array 3 before and after its 3 Sep realignment. 14–16 Oct: Fennick stock ran short and counters 1–12 used Brackwater stock from stores; those tags failed at 1.6%, while kiosk tags issued the same days failed at 12.1%. Engineer's note (T. Rhee): sampled no-read images show faint, broken bars; the images cannot show whether the media or the printer heat setting is responsible.
34	C10 [stage S1] Interview notes with three Tessaly evening-bank crew leads, 7 Nov - Corvane quality officer (staff-account): All three leads said the evening bank has been 'tight' since the two new departures and that they are short by one or two loaders on some nights. Lead A: 'We close the cart at minus 35 like we're told. Bags keep coming down after that and we get blamed.' Lead B said check-in 'sends us more rush bags than Quillon ever mentioned'. Lead C thought new staff were sometimes slow building containers. None of them could say how many bags arrived after closure.
35	C11 [stage S1] Corvane baggage service desk mishandling cause codes, Harlow Bay, Aug–Oct - Corvane baggage service desk records (system-record): Cause codes are assigned by baggage service agents (Quillon staff in Aug, Tessaly staff from Sep) when a passenger reports a missing bag, before the bag is traced. Share of departing-bag mishandles, Aug/Sep/Oct: 'failure to load' 34%, 52%, 55%; 'late check-in' 14%, 9%, 8%; 'tagging error' 11%, 8%, 7%; 'transfer short-connection' 22%, 17%, 16%; 'other/unknown' 19%, 14%, 14%. Corvane's coding guide defines 'failure to load' as 'bag available at the lateral but not loaded'. Agents say the guide is 'rarely consulted'.
36	C12 [stage S1] HBAA manual encode desk staffing roster and rated throughput, Jul–Oct - Harlow Bay Airport Authority baggage operations (system-record): Manual encode desk, baggage hall level -1. Staffing: two encoders per shift on all shifts, July through October; no vacancy or sickness gap longer than one shift in any month. Rated throughput: about 22 bags per hour per encoder when the tag is partly legible, and 12 per hour when the bag must be matched by passenger name. The desk is staffed by HBAA, not by any ground handler. A third workstation exists and can be staffed with seven days' notice.
37	C13 [stage S1] Corvane–Tessaly handling agreement: SLA schedule and draft penalty calculation, Sep–Oct - Corvane finance and legal (financial-record): SLA 4.2: departing mishandled bags per 1,000 passengers not to exceed 4.5 in any month, measured on the Corvane dashboard. Exclusions cover 'causes outside the handler's reasonable control, including airport infrastructure'. The performance element is 8% of the monthly fee. Corvane finance's draft calculation puts the withholding for Sep and Oct at €186,000 in total. Clause 19: a breach notice triggers a 60-day cure period and allows Corvane to retender.
38	C14 [stage S1] Kiosk maintenance vendor service reports, Harlow Bay, Aug–Oct - Kiosk maintenance contractor (vendor-account): Callouts for kiosk tag-printer faults: Aug 14, Sep 31, Oct 29. Resolution recorded for each callout: 'media path cleared, test print OK'. Fault cause field: 'not determined' on 52 of the 60 Sep–Oct callouts and 'label debris on platen' on 8. Technicians did not record which tag stock was loaded. Preventive cleaning has been carried out fortnightly since 1 Sep under the revised contract.
39	C15 [stage S1] Harlow Bay weather and air traffic flow restriction summary, Aug–Oct - Regional air navigation service and met office summary (external-data): Days with flow restrictions affecting Harlow Bay departures: Aug 6, Sep 4, Oct 5. Thunderstorm ramp closures (lightning stop): Aug, 5 events totalling 6.2 hours; Sep, 2 events totalling 1.5 hours; Oct, none. Days with wind above loading limits: Oct 2. Restrictions applied to all carriers equally.
40	C16 [stage S1] Tessaly Ground mishandling performance at its other contracted airports, Jan–Oct - Tessaly Ground commercial team (vendor-account): Tessaly-supplied summary for four other airports where it has handled for more than two years: departing mishandled bags per 1,000 passengers stayed between 3.1 and 4.4 at every station in every month, with no rise in Sep–Oct. Tessaly notes that new-station start-ups 'typically see a small rise for six to eight weeks'. The figures are Tessaly's own and have not been verified by the customers concerned.
41	CANDIDATES
42	H1: The changeover to Tessaly Ground put less experienced crews on Corvane's turns, and their handling failures are causing the rise in Corvane's mishandled-bag rate at Harlow Bay.
43	H2: A change in how Corvane's bag tags are produced at Harlow Bay check-in has reduced automatic tag reading in the baggage system, and the extra bags diverted to manual encoding are missing their flights.
44	H3: Corvane's added evening departures have compressed baggage handling on the evening bank enough to cause the rise in mishandled bags.
45	H4: Deterioration of the airport baggage system's tag-scanning equipment has reduced automatic tag reading, and the extra bags diverted to manual encoding are missing their flights.
46	H5: The tag stock supplied by Fennick Labels is defective as manufactured, so it would read poorly even with correctly adjusted printers.
47	R1: Handler changeover to Tessaly Ground on 1 Sep -> Rise in Corvane bags not carried on the booked flight (causes)
48	R2: Switch to Fennick Labels tag stock at Harlow Bay check-in on 1 Sep -> Rise in automatic tag-read failures for Corvane bags (causes)
49	R3: Rise in Corvane bags diverted to manual encoding -> Rise in Corvane bags not carried on the booked flight (causes)
50	R4: Switch to Fennick Labels tag stock at Harlow Bay check-in on 1 Sep -> Rise in tag-printer jam/misfeed tickets (causes)
51	A1: Issue Tessaly Ground a formal breach notice and withhold the performance element of its fee for September and October.
52	A2: Return Harlow Bay counters and kiosks to Brackwater tag stock now, while the Fennick stock is tested separately.
53	A3: Lodge a formal defect claim with Fennick Labels seeking replacement of the delivered batches and recovery of mishandling costs.
54	A4: Ask HBAA to staff an additional manual-encode workstation during the evening bank as a temporary measure.

57	I2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]

64	I9: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]

answers.justification: Pelion bags are worked by the same Tessaly crew pool, and Pelion's rate stayed flat at 3.6–3.8. Corvane's auto-read-path rate also stayed flat at 3.7–3.9. The whole rise is in manual-encode bags that reached the lateral after it closed (C4). Training records were clean (C1).

No-read rates rose from 1.5% on Brackwater tags to 11.8% on Fennick tags, while transfer and Pelion tags stayed flat on every array. On 14–16 Oct the same counters reverted to Brackwater stock and failed at only 1.6% (C9). The extra encode bags miss their flights (C4).

Evening-bank passenger volume fell (C6). The auto-read-path rate was unchanged (C4). The rise is confined to tag-read failures, which are explained by the tag stock (C9), so evening compression is at most a minor contributor.
Transfer and Pelion tags read at 1.3–1.4% on every array, including array 3 before and after its realignment (C9). Maintenance was done on schedule (C5).

The engineer says the no-read images cannot separate a media fault from printer heat settings (C9). Darkness adjustment for a new supplier's media is plausible (C8), and the only test certificate is Fennick's own (C7). So a manufacturing defect is live but not established.
The changeover coincides in time with the rise (E1), but Pelion changed handler on the same day with the same crew pool and saw no rise. The auto-read-path rate under Tessaly is unchanged (C4).

The 14–16 Oct counter reversion to Brackwater stock is a natural experiment: same counters and printers, failure rate 1.6%, while Fennick kiosk tags failed at 12.1% (C9). Reader faults are ruled out by the flat transfer and Pelion rates (C9).

The encode-path rate rose from 0.2 to about 4 while the auto-read path stayed flat. Encode volume rose about 6.5-fold and evening dwell rose from 7 to 33 minutes. 91% of failed bags reached the lateral after closing. Their check-in timing matches auto-read bags, which rules out late check-in (C4).

Jam tickets rose with the stock change (E5). But kiosk preventive cleaning was cut to fortnightly at the same time, tickets are not split by counter versus kiosk, and stock type was not recorded (E5, C14).

The evidence points to the tag stock rather than handling (C4, C9). The SLA excludes causes outside the handler's control (C13). A breach notice would punish the wrong party and could trigger a retender.

Brackwater stock is on hand (about 5 weeks) and its contract runs to 31 Dec (E5). It read at 1.6% in the October reversion (C9). Reverting removes the cause quickly and can be undone, while Fennick stock and printer settings are tested (C8).
Whether the fault lies in the media or the printer darkness settings is unresolved (C9, C8). A defect claim depends on H5, which is not yet confirmed (C7).
A third encode workstation is available on seven days' notice (C12) and would cut evening dwell (C4). But it treats the symptom, and reverting the stock (A2) fixes the cause sooner.
The natural experiment and carrier controls (C9, C4) are enough to commit to the low-risk, reversible stock reversion (A2).
